feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 8 (0.6 kg, otherwise iteration 5) is the best measured design at 257.45. Lowering mass from 0.8 to 0.6 kg raised oval progress from 0.71 to 0.89, brought oval finishes to 10 of 20, reduced oval oscillation from 0.327 to 0.316, and lowered s-bend and slalom max_error to 0.0603 and 0.0615 m, with line losses still 0. Yaw inertia is therefore a working lever that does not touch the sensors. Iteration 5 (0.8 kg) remains the reference for these comparisons. Iteration 6 (16 mm footprint) cut oval progress to 0.51 and iteration 7 (inner sensors at ±0.04 m) cut it to 0.22, so neither geometry should be retried. This candidate continues the mass trend to 0.5 kg. If the next race shows oval progress at or above 0.8 with oscillation at or below 0.33 and line losses at 0, keep lowering mass in small steps. If oval progress falls below 0.5 or oscillation rises above 0.33, the lighter robot is overshooting, so return to 0.6 kg. If s-bend and slalom still reach about 0.060 m with losses at 0, the mass gain has flattened, so the controller response is the next limit to address, not the geometry.
requested_changes: Set mass to 0.5 kg with the iteration 8 layout unchanged (outer ±0.06 m, inner ±0.03 m, y 0.04 m, 12 mm footprints, 12 cm track, 3 cm radius). Iteration 8 showed mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg raised oval progress from 0.71 to 0.89 and lowered s-bend and slalom max_error, so the trend is measured, not guessed.

If oval progress falls below 0.5 or oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.33 (iteration 8 gave 0.316), return mass to 0.6 kg, since iteration 8 is the best measured design and lost oval progress costs more than edge gain.

Do not retry inner ±0.04 m (iteration 7 oval progress 0.22), sensor_size 0.016 m (iteration 6 oval progress 0.51), wheel_track 0.10 m (iteration 3 oval progress 0.14) or y 0.06 m (iteration 4 oval progress 0.20). Each was rejected by earlier evidence.
